items.title: JWST finds a possible black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy in the early universe
items.summary: How the first massive black holes formed in the universe remains an open question in astronomy. Black holes weighing about a billion solar masses within the first billion years of the universe require extraordinary origin stories.

items.title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
items.summary: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet's mountain of mysteries.

items.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
items.summary: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat Sunday after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey.

items.title: Hybrid nanocrystal surface reveals new way to tune interactions with infrared light
items.summary: A one-crystal-thick sheet made from two types of nanocrystals mixed in solution can amplify or suppress infrared light beyond the sum of its parts.

items.title: Milky Way simulation reaches record resolution with the help of three supercomputers
items.summary: A team of researchers, including those from the University of Tokyo, have developed a new way to model the Milky Way at a level of detail never achieved before. items.title: Parasite makes mice more attractive to blood-feeding bugs, which may aid its spread
items.summary: Some parasites, such as Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi, can be passed between mammals and blood-feeding insects called triatomine bugs. Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs.

items.title: Novo istraživanje dovodi u pitanje ono što se govori o djeci i ekranima
items.summary: FINSKA studija otkrila da više vremena pred ekranom u djetinjstvu može dovesti do boljih kognitivnih sposobnosti u adolescenciji, naglašavajući važnost kvalitete sadržaja, a ne samo količine.

items.title: The avian champions of long-distance migration keep surprising scientists
items.summary: "The whole story began with an extinct bird from Hispaniola," said Min Zhao, a former postdoctoral associate at the Florida Museum of Natural History (now a postdoctoral researcher at Uppsala University).

items.title: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down
items.summary: Most materials get weaker with use. But a team led by Chenfeng Ke, a professor of chemistry in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, has created a polymer that defies the usual laws of wear and tear.

items.title: Dropping degree requirements linked to higher pay for workers without degrees
items.summary: The requirements set by human resources (HR) greatly influence the professional opportunities available to different segments of the population.
